question: How can someone pay a loan every single month and still owe more each year?
answer: When the payments are smaller than the interest. A €20,000 loan at 6% adds €1,200 of interest a year; paying €80 a month covers only €960, so the balance grows by €240, and next year's interest is charged on the larger sum. Compounding works on debts too: the borrower pays faithfully while the balance climbs.
move: Check that a payment beats the interest before calling it progress.
ask: Do my monthly payments on what I owe actually cover more than the interest?
reference: Brealey, Myers & Allen, Principles of Corporate Finance, 13th edition, McGraw-Hill, 2020
